# Saltwater Long Range Trip Planner

> Self-contained HTML dashboard for planning long-range saltwater fishing trips out of San Diego:
> aggregates trips from 11 long-range boats into a filterable Trip Finder, derives a Processing Planner of
> boat returns per day (long-range + multi-day boats from the four SD landings), and adds a Processing Calculator comparing two San Diego fish processors.
> Pure HTML/CSS/JS in one file — no server, no build step.

## Start here
- [BUILD-PLAN.md](BUILD-PLAN.md): the data-refresh design. §1–10 the 2026-09 multi-day work (decisions, data sources, safety nets, the task's contract in §10.3, phase results); §11 the 2026-11 long-range + processor-rate extension (decisions D8–D13).
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): canonical agent guide — file map, data contract (`RAW`, `MULTI`, `data/`), verification gates, scraping protocol, weekly refresh, Node dependency layout.
- [README.md](README.md): human quickstart — features, usage, data sources, refresh instructions.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): version history, newest first.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): commit + README standard.

## Dashboard
- [index.html](index.html): GitHub Pages entry point — redirects to the dashboard file below.
- [saltwater_trip_planner.html](saltwater_trip_planner.html): the entire dashboard — Trip Finder, Processing Planner, and Processing Calculator tabs. Long-range trip data lives in the auto-generated `RAW` block (return dates derived from departure + trip length); multi-day rows live in the auto-generated `MULTI` block (return date/time as posted). Two self-checking freshness stamps, `#lr-stamp` and `#multi-stamp`. Tests: `node test-multiday.js`, `python3 tests/test_refresh_multiday.py`.

## Refresh
- [refresh_multiday.py](refresh_multiday.py): headless refresh of BOTH trip-data blocks — the four landings into the MULTI-DAY block and all 11 long-range boats into the `RAW` block. Writes data/; `--skip-longrange` does multi-day only; tests in tests/.
- [check_rates.py](check_rates.py): compares both fish processors' published cash rates to the dashboard's `PROCESSORS` and writes data/rates_check.json. Reports only — never edits the dashboard.

## Key rules
- The `MULTI` and `RAW` blocks are both written only by `refresh_multiday.py` (Sunday task `saltwater-multiday-refresh`); never hand-edit between their markers. `BOATS` stays hand-maintained and must keep the same order as the script's `BOAT_SOURCES`.
- A refresh must preserve what the boat pages cannot supply: the `'ed'` trip flag, curated trip names (matched on boatIdx + departure date), and trips that already departed.
- A long-range row whose fields do not all parse cleanly keeps its previous values and is counted as `unresolved`; never publish a guessed trip field.
- Processing rates in `PROCESSORS` are CASH figures — `calcQuotes` adds each processor's `ccFee` on top, so a credit-column value charges the fee twice. `check_rates.py` must report no change after any rate edit.
- Interactive sessions leave the tree clean, or the Sunday preflight aborts (`dirty-tree`).
- Single self-contained HTML file: all CSS/JS inline, opens via file://, no external dependencies, no localStorage (in-memory state only).
- Never add a `package.json` to this repo. The test harness's `jsdom` (and tooling's `docx`) are declared in the parent Cowork folder's manifest; run `npm install` / `npm test` from there. Never `npm install <pkg> --no-save` in that folder — it prunes the packages it was not asked for.
- Trip data is a snapshot — every refresh must update the visible "data as of" disclaimer and README data-freshness note, and link to live sources.
- fishingreservations.net blocks rapid automated requests (CAPTCHA error 338): send a browser User-Agent and space requests 1.5 s apart, as both scripts do. All 15 sources load headlessly (landings verified 2026-09-03, all 11 boats 2026-11-08). Reading pre-loaded browser tabs is the repair path if a page starts refusing, not the weekly job.
- Long-range rows (`RAW` block, auto-generated): return dates are derived from departure + trip length. Multi-day rows (MULTI block, auto-generated): return date/time are stored as posted by the landing. Never hand-edit either block.
- Push with plain `git push origin main` from this clone (decision D7; git and gh are already logged in on Ed's Mac, no PAT). The GitHub Contents API is only for a sandbox where git cannot run — there, GET the file sha first, then PUT with sha, or you get a 409.
- Data refresh commits use the `data` type with a body of at least 3 bullets; README updated on every feat/fix/data commit.
